body:
Second stage of the bounded pre-auth slots (audit findings F1, F2, F6; design: `security-design-lua-editmode-and-preauth-slots` Part 2, approved 2026-10-15). Builds on #168 (`Connection`), #171 (the policy classes), #153 (deadlines). **No protocol change** (`allowProtocol` stays false).

## What changes

- **Acceptor thread** (today's server thread): accept, make non-blocking, read the peer, ask the rate limiter (a backed-off address is closed at once), take a **pre-auth slot** (`PreAuthSlots`: N in all, 2 per non-loopback address, loopback may use all) and a **handshake token** (`TokenBucket`: 20/s in all, 5/s per address; excess closed before TLS), queue the connection for a worker. A refused connection is closed at once, with no TLS and no log line; the refusals are counted and reported in one summary line every 10 s. It is also the only thread that re-reads the tokens file (every 100 ms wait slice, so a SIGHUP revoking the session's user still ends that session).
- **N pre-auth workers** (`--preauth-slots`, default 4, 1-16): TLS handshake (5 s budget), then **one** Hello frame (64 KiB cap, 2 s budget); the token and protocol major version are verified **on the worker** (`EvaluateHello`, factored out of `HandleHello` and shared); the rate-limit outcome (failures, unfinished Hellos) is recorded before the socket is closed; a refusal is answered on the worker. Then the connection is offered to the session.
- **One session thread**: runs the session (the existing request loop with the idle/write/age deadlines) and on exit does today's cleanup. It **replays** the worker's Hello payload through the ordinary `ExecuteCommand(Hello)` on the main thread, so identity, `ServerInfo`, `_clientErrorCodes` and the edit-group/key side effects are exactly as before; if the token was revoked meanwhile the replay refuses and the connection closes. After a successful replay it re-checks the identity against the tokens table (closes the window in which a reload lands between the Hello's check and the identity it bound).
- **Busy** (this stage: a plain Error): a second authenticated client waits up to 1 s for the active session (one that is just ending), then gets "The host is serving another session; try again later" and is closed. No `ErrorCoded` `busy`, no preemption, no takeover (S-4); `SessionArbiter` is not used. **Behaviour change:** before this the second client waited in the backlog without limit.
- A host **without a token** keeps one-at-a-time as before (no Hello, no Busy): a second connection waits in a worker, holding a slot.
- `listen(s, N + 4)`; `Stop()` joins the acceptor, every worker and the session thread (each polls `_running` every 100 ms; no wait without it), then closes what it still holds.
- `--preauth-slots <n>` (validation, usage, docs); a startup line states the limits.
- **EINTR decided and fixed** (S-1 left it open): an interrupted `poll`/`WSAPoll` (a signal such as SIGHUP lands on any thread now) is a wait that found nothing and is retried, not a failed wait.
- Per-connection state stays in `Connection`; a `ConnectionPtr` closes a connection (TLS, then socket) when its last owner lets go, so no early return or exception leaks a socket, and a slot is freed after its connection is closed.
- Pre-auth logging: nothing for a connection refused at accept; "Waiting for editor connection..." once (and after each session) instead of per accept; "Editor connected/disconnected" belong to sessions. A connection that gets a slot and then fails still writes the lines it wrote before (bounded by the handshake rate and the budgets); the "Refused Hello" line is written before the refusal reaches the client (`PostLogAndWait`, at most 500 ms), as it was when the main thread refused the Hello.

## Shared state (reviewer list)

tokens table: `shared_ptr` swap under `_tokensMutex` (acceptor), copy elsewhere; `ReloadTokens` bookkeeping acceptor-only. `RateLimiter`/`PreAuthSlots`/`TokenBucket`: own mutex, no call out under it. Job queue and hand-off slot: a mutex + condvar each; a session is "active" from the moment its hand-off is taken (same lock) until it ends. Session identity/close flag: cleared together under `_identityMutex` at session start/end; `CheckIdentityAgainstTokens` reads the identity and sets the flag under the same lock (order: tokens snapshot, then identity; never the reverse). TLS config read-only after `Start` (random generator locked by Mbed TLS). Logging via `PostLog`. Engine state main thread only.

## Tests

New `tests/editor-server/PreAuthServerTests.cpp` (real loopback sockets, fake peers via `SetPeerAddressProvider`): stalled/silent peers in the other slots do not block an authenticated client, a full house leaves a running session alone, a session answers through 100 connect/close cycles, the N+1th connection and the 3rd from one address are closed at once with no line, slot release on every path, summary line, handshake bucket on a moved clock, Busy, a host without a token serves one at a time, replay equivalence (`ServerInfo` bytes equal `ExecuteCommand(Hello)`, error codes per connection), a refused Hello never becomes a session, `Stop()` with a session + silent peers + a client waiting in a worker, restart, settings. `EditorTlsTests`: stalled TLS handshakes do not block a TLS client; four concurrent handshakes. `EditorTokensTests`: a token revoked between the worker check and the replay (a test hook holds the worker). `HostOptionsTests`: `--preauth-slots`. Docs: `logging-and-editor.html` (new "Pre-auth slots" section, rate-limit gaps corrected only where now true), `editor.html`, `testing.html`.

**Existing tests changed (two):** (one) `EditorTlsServerTest.ASlowHandshakeHasItsOwnFiveSecondsAndTheHelloBudgetStartsWhenItEnds` waited for the pre-auth "Editor connected" line to know the server had read the end-of-handshake time; a pre-auth connection no longer writes that line (deliberate, item 9), so it waits for three more reads of the injected clock. **(two)** `PreHelloAccountingTest.EveryWayOutWithoutAHelloCountsAsAFailure` relied on the one serving thread having counted each broken-in connection before the next was accepted; the pre-auth connections are served concurrently now (a third connection from one address while two still hold its slots is closed at accept, uncounted), so it waits for each connection to be admitted and its slot freed (a failure is counted before the slot is freed) via a new `PreAuthAdmittedConnections()` seam. No other existing test was edited; the rest passed unchanged on all 10 CI checks.

## Deviations / judgement calls

- Busy grace: an authenticated client waits up to 1 s (`DefaultBusyGrace`) before it is told Busy; without it a client reconnecting as its last connection closes is turned away by a session that has ended but not finished its cleanup (and most existing tests would flake).
- The handshake bucket is **off in the class** (`SetHandshakeRateLimit(nullopt)`) and **on in `N2EditorHost`** (20/s, 5/s per address): existing fake-peer fixtures make 6-12 connections from one pretend address in a second.
- No-token host: second connection waits in a worker with no limit (holding a slot) instead of Busy, per the brief; a peer that closes while waiting is not noticed until it is handed off.
- Fake peers use `SetPeerAddressProvider` (the existing seam), not `SetAcceptedSocketHook`.
- A summary interval setter, a pre-hand-off hook and counters (`PreAuthRefusedConnections`, `BusyRefusals`, `SessionHandoffs`, `PreAuthSlotsInUse`) were added as test seams.
- The worker does not call `RecordSuccess`: the replay does (as before), so a Busy client does not clear its address's failures.
- A replay refusal (token revoked in between) is counted as a wrong token by the session path, as the main-thread Hello always was.

## Not verified

- No sanitizer (TSan/ASan) run exists or was run: data races and lock order are reasoned about and tested on CI, not proven.
- Windows thread/socket behaviour (WSAPoll across threads, closing/destroying sockets from the owning thread) is only what the Windows CI legs exercise.
- A real signal (EINTR) during a wait: no test sends one.
- Concurrent handshakes on one shared Mbed TLS configuration and key (relies on `MBEDTLS_THREADING_C`); one test makes four at once.
- Slot memory (about 150 KiB, an estimate), handshake CPU under a real flood, behaviour behind NAT/a proxy.
- Nothing was built or run locally beyond syntax checks; CI (all 10 checks green on the final head) is the evidence.
